cohort: Eighty-four preterm infants born by cesarean section were prospectively enrolled, with 28 experiencing infections, feeding intolerance, or NEC (diseased group) and 56 serving as a control group.
finding: Diseased infants had lower gestational age and birth weight, longer hospitalization, and significant differences in meconium microbial composition compared to controls, specifically with a higher abundance of p_Firmicutes in the disease group.
cross-section timing: First-pass meconium samples collected shortly after birth.
birth_weight: Preterm infants; diseased infants had significantly lower body weight compared to controls.
gest_age: Preterm infants; diseased infants had significantly lower gestational age compared to controls.
